ruling_1_text_to_motion.seam_blend_how: 58_loop_blend.py search: every window on the clip's own keys (strafes 36-59 / 24-59 intervals, the run its one trimmed cycle), blend 3-20 intervals, modes pre / post (cross-fade into the source's own lead-in or run-on) / offset (a growing correction onto the start pose); scored by the SUPPORT toe's world slide inside the blend (the lower toe, same foot, body driven at the loop's foot-lock speed), then the loop's p95. ruling_4_the_run_slide.finding: NOT a regression in the clip. Two things in the scene, both measured (tools/run_trace.gd):
ruling_4_the_run_slide.one_phase_lock: T12_8's run was 16 intervals at 24 fps (0.6667 s); the probe steps at exactly 1/24 s, so every cycle it sampled the SAME 16 phases (the clip position repeated to 0.0001 s: 0.2969, 0.5886 ...). Only two of those phases passed the probe's pair rule -- 7 pairs in 60 frames -- and the median was the median of those two. T12_9's run is 19 intervals at 30 fps (0.6333 s, 15.2 frames per cycle): the phases drift, the pairs sample the whole stance (14-16 pairs), including toe-off frames, and the median rises (22.6 / 24.1 mm)
ruling_4_the_run_slide.two_the_import_bake: Godot's glTF importer BAKES every animation at the import fps (animation/fps=30 in every .import here): T12_8's 24 fps run was resampled a second time in the engine -- its toes ran up to 3.05 cm (median 0.72 cm) off the file, exact only where the two grids meet (every 1/6 s). T12_9's 30 fps run plays as filed (0.21 cm max). Every 24 fps track still in the GLB is re-baked on import (attack, the weapon_r channel tracks, the pose clips' 1/24 s second key)
ruling_4_the_run_slide.the_clips_themselves: the same pair rule over all phases at the drive speed (5.141 m/s, 1/24 s, 8 start phases): T12_8 ~19 pairs at 20.9 mm, T12_9 ~16 at 18.6-20.3 mm -- the re-cut run slides slightly LESS. Its foot-lock (s6's pooled median, toes) is 5.260 m/s against the drive 5.141 (2.3%)
ruling_4_the_run_slide.correction_to_T12_9_record: T12_9's measure.json reported foot-lock as the MEAN of the two feet's medians (walk 1.581/1.610, run 3.984/5.196); s6 pools both feet: walk 1.583/1.602, run 3.952/5.260 (57_footlock.py now pools)
